name: Rondonia
summary_text: Rondônia stands under the national framework of Brazil, where same-sex marriage has been legal nationwide since the National Council of Justice Resolution of 14 May 2013, adopted by a 14-1 vote, with joint adoption permitted since 2010 and full marital rights since 2015. The Supreme Federal Tribunal ruling of 1 March 2018 removed surgery, hormone therapy and diagnosis as conditions for legal gender-marker change, and the age of consent is equal regardless of sexual orientation.  On 13 June 2019 the Supreme Federal Court held in ADO 26 and MI 4733 that discrimination and violence on grounds of sexual orientation or gender identity constitute a crime equivalent to racism under Law 7.716/1989, carrying imprisonment of one to five years and fines. Federal anti-discrimination provisions cover sexual-orientation and gender-identity grounds, so a trans visitor's documents and entry are assessed under the same rules as anyone else's.  Documents remain the sharpest friction. There is no third-gender option in national identity documents, although civil-registry entries marked non-binary or unspecified have been possible since 2020, and a Superior Court of Justice ruling of 6 May 2025 allows rectification of gender to a neutral marker and treats the decision as precedent. Gender-marker change otherwise proceeds by self-determination.  Risk of violence does not track the statute. Brazil retains one of the world's highest rates of violence against sexual and gender minorities, most acutely affecting trans people, and enforcement of the protections is uneven in practice. The advances themselves face repeal pressure from a conservative Congress.  Political visibility is measurable. Salabert and Hilton became the country's first transgender federal legislators in 2022, and more than 3,000 openly LGBTQ candidates stood in the 2024 municipal elections.
